title: 015 — Review of a pallet-count discrepancy

plan.situation: Ternwood Supplies (contact Yara Pell) shipped 24 cartons, C01–C24, on 3 pallets (P1–P3) under VEL-015-26 to Marshglass intake. Marshglass signed for 4 handling units (H1–H4) on sheet RC-015. Yara reads this as a mismatch and wants a missing-pallet claim recorded. The record shows the transit depot repacked the 3 pallets into 4 handling units on 2026-10-13, and every carton is mapped to a unit. So 3 versus 4 is a difference in the unit counted, not evidence that a pallet is missing. But the receiving sheet only covers handling units, and there is no carton-level receiving scan, so we cannot yet confirm that the whole order arrived.

facts.fact: VEL-015-26: 24 cartons C01–C24 shipped on original pallets P1–P3 to Marshglass intake; contact Yara Pell; reconciliation channel freight@vellora.example
Guide F15: compare counts in the same unit; repacking may change pallet or handling-unit counts; carton IDs are the basis for reconciliation; receiving signatures attest only the fields shown
Carton mapping recorded before receipt puts all 24 cartons on H1–H4, 6 each: H1 = C01–C06, H2 = C07–C12, H3 = C13–C18, H4 = C19–C24
P1 held C01–C08, P2 held C09–C16, P3 held C17–C24; repack mapping recorded 2026-10-13; carton labels kept on each new handling unit
H1–H4 were created at the transit depot; the receiving sheet reports handling units only; no carton-level receiving scan has been supplied
Receiving sheet RC-015: H1, H2, H3, H4 received, 4 handling units, received 2026-10-14 07:50 +01:00, signed by Iven Reed (IR-15), Marshglass intake
Yara Pell says three pallets were sent, four units were signed for, and asks for a missing-pallet claim
The 3-pallet versus 4-unit gap is explained by the documented repack and does not by itself show a missing pallet
Whether all 24 cartons were physically received at Marshglass has not been confirmed at carton level

conflicts: Yara Pell sees 3 pallets shipped versus 4 units signed for as a discrepancy (E04). The records show the 3 pallets were repacked into 4 handling units with every carton mapped (E03, E05, E06), so the counts use different units. Carton-level receipt is still unconfirmed, so this is routed to the reconciliation desk for a carton-level count rather than settled either way.
missing_information: A carton-level receiving count or scan from Marshglass intake for C01–C24 across H1–H4
Whether carton labels C01–C24 were present on H1–H4 when received
risk_flags: Customer is asking for a loss claim that the unit-count difference does not support; recording it now would rest on comparing two different units
Receiving signature IR-15 covers handling units only (F15); it cannot be treated as proof that all 24 cartons arrived
No outcome, claim acceptance or compensation will be promised

authority_map.controls: Carton-level reconciliation of VEL-015-26 and getting the receiving count from Marshglass intake
What was physically received and what the receiving sheet attests
Whether any missing-goods claim is opened or accepted (no claim is warranted on current evidence)
Requests on behalf of the shipper; no authority over the receiving record

wait_check.new_since_last_promise: No earlier desk promise. E07 restates the E04 request and asks for a decision; E05 and E06 add repack evidence that has not yet been acted on.

plan.decision_summary: Do not record a missing-pallet claim on the 3-versus-4 count, which the repack explains. Ask the Vellora reconciliation desk for a carton-level receiving count of C01–C24 from Marshglass intake, and tell Yara Pell where things stand without confirming full receipt.
plan.rationale: Guide F15 says carton IDs are the basis for reconciliation, and the recorded repack mapping accounts for all 24 cartons across H1–H4. So 3 pallets becoming 4 handling units is not evidence of loss. But the receiving sheet only attests to handling units, so whether the whole order arrived can only be answered with a carton-level receiving record. The reconciliation desk owns that record and has a recorded channel. Yara asked for a decision, so she gets an honest interim answer.

actions.subject: VEL-015-26 – carton-level receiving count needed for C01–C24 (sheet RC-015)
actions.purpose: Get the carton-level proof that settles whether the whole order arrived
actions.body:
Hello,

Re: VEL-015-26 (Ternwood Supplies to Marshglass intake). Receiving sheet RC-015 (received 2026-10-14 07:50 +01:00, signed IR-15) lists only handling units H1–H4, count 4. Your ledger (E06) shows H1–H4 were created at the transit depot from original pallets P1–P3, and the repack mapping recorded on 2026-10-13 assigns cartons C01–C24 across H1–H4 (6 per unit).

The shipper is asking whether a pallet is missing. Under guide F15, carton IDs are the basis for reconciliation, and no carton-level receiving scan is in the packet. Could you please obtain from Marshglass intake, or from your own records, a carton-level receiving count or scan showing which of C01–C24 were received on H1–H4, and confirm whether the carton labels were present on receipt? Please reply within today's working day with the record or its expected time.

This is a request for a record. We have not opened or confirmed any claim.

Thank you,
Rivet Delivery Desk

actions.subject: VEL-015-26 – your three pallets and the four units signed for
actions.purpose: Give the requester an accurate interim answer to her decision request
actions.body:
Dear Yara,

Thank you for your messages about VEL-015-26. On the way to Marshglass, your 24 cartons (C01–C24) were repacked at the transit depot from your three pallets (P1–P3) onto four handling units (H1–H4). The repack record maps every carton to one of these four units. That is why Marshglass signed for four units. On its own, the change from three to four does not show that a pallet is missing.

However, Marshglass's receiving sheet only counts handling units, not individual cartons. So we cannot yet confirm that all 24 cartons arrived. We have asked our reconciliation team for a carton-level receiving count. We will update you once we have it. If any carton turns out to be unaccounted for, we will take up the claim with you at that point.

Kind regards,
Rivet Delivery Desk

Check whether the reconciliation desk has supplied the carton-level receiving count for C01–C24. If not, chase via freight@vellora.example. If the count shows any carton missing, or the desk cannot produce it, move to investigations with the record.

Not confirming the whole order arrived: the receiving signature covers handling units only, and there is no carton-level scan
Not promising any compensation, outcome or timing that the reconciliation desk has not given
Not contacting receiver Iven Reed directly; this goes through the recorded reconciliation channel
plan.follow_up: Check at the end of the working day on 2026-10-14 for the carton-level receiving count. If there is no reply, chase freight@vellora.example. If cartons are missing or the record cannot be produced, refer the case to investigations, and only then consider a claim, subject to human approval.

issues.problem: The message to Yara is labelled action_class 'request_record_or_statement', but it actually gives her an interim status update and asks her for nothing.
issues.fix: Change the action_class to a status or interim update class.

issues.problem: case_parameters list requester_type as 'consumer', but Ternwood Supplies is a business shipper. They also set evidence_conflict to false, even though the plan itself lists a conflict between Yara's claim and the repack records.
issues.fix: Set requester_type to business/shipper and set evidence_conflict to true, or make the two fields consistent with the conflicts section.

issues.problem: The email to the reconciliation desk cites the internal event label '(E06)'. That label means nothing to the person reading the email.
issues.fix: Refer to it as the repacking ledger entry of 08:40 instead.

review.summary: The plan reads the 3-pallet vs 4-unit gap correctly as a change of unit caused by the documented repack (F15, E03, E05, E06). It refuses to open a missing-pallet claim and also refuses to confirm full receipt, because the receiving signature covers handling units only. It asks the owning reconciliation desk for a carton-level count and gives Yara an honest interim answer that is grounded in the records. The only issues are minor labelling ones.
